chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdullah al-Barqi from his father from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. Umar from Abu al-Jarud from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju'fi from Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari. He said:

Amir al-Mu'minin Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) delivered a sermon to us. He praised Allah and commended Him, then said: O people! In front of this pulpit of yours are four men from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) -- among them: Anas b. Malik, al-Bara' b. Azib al-Ansari, al-Ash'ath b. Qays al-Kindi, and Khalid b. Yazid al-Bajali. Then he turned his face toward Anas b. Malik and said: O Anas! If you had heard the Messenger of Allah say: 'Whoever I was his master, then this Ali is his master,' yet you did not bear witness to my wilaya today, then may Allah not cause you to die until He afflicts you with a leprosy that the turban cannot cover. As for you, O Ash'ath, if you had heard the Messenger of Allah say: 'Whoever I was his master, then this Ali is his master. O Allah! Befriend whoever befriends him and oppose whoever opposes him,' yet you did not bear witness to my wilaya today, then may Allah not cause you to die until both your eyes go blind. As for you, O Khalid b. Yazid, if you had heard the Messenger of Allah say the same, yet you did not bear witness today, then may Allah not cause you to die except the death of Jahiliyya. As for you, O Bara' b. Azib, if you had heard the Messenger of Allah say the same, yet you did not bear witness today, then may Allah not cause you to die except in the place from which you emigrated.

Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari said: By Allah, I saw Anas b. Malik afflicted with leprosy, trying to cover it with a turban but unable to hide it. And I saw al-Ash'ath b. Qays with both his eyes gone blind, saying: 'Praise be to Allah who made Amir al-Mu'minin Ali b. Abi Talib pray against me with blindness in this world, and did not pray against me with punishment in the Hereafter so that I be punished.' As for Khalid b. Yazid -- he died, and his family wanted to bury him. They dug a grave for him in his house and buried him. When Kindah heard about it, they came with horses and camels and slaughtered them at the door of his house; so he died the death of Jahiliyya. As for al-Bara' b. Azib, Mu'awiya appointed him over Yemen, and he died there -- which is the place from which he had emigrated.

key_terms.الولاية: Wilaya -- authority, guardianship, the concept of divinely-appointed leadership central to Shi'a theology
key_terms.برص: Baras -- leprosy, the affliction invoked against Anas b. Malik for refusing to testify
key_terms.كريمتيك: Karimatayк -- your two precious ones (i.e., your eyes), the affliction invoked against al-Ash'ath
key_terms.مولاه: Mawla -- master, patron, guardian; the key term in the Ghadir declaration establishing Ali's authority
key_terms.ميتة جاهلية: Death of Jahiliyya -- dying in the manner of pre-Islamic paganism, the worst form of death in Islamic eschatology

ai.seo_question: What happened to the companions who refused to testify at Ghadir Khumm according to Shi'a hadith?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Amali of al-Saduq records Imam Ali's sermon in which he confronted four companions -- Anas b. Malik, al-Bara' b. Azib, al-Ash'ath b. Qays, and Khalid b. Yazid -- who had heard the Prophet's Ghadir Khumm declaration ('Whoever I was his master, then Ali is his master') but refused to testify to Ali's wilaya. Each was given a specific imprecation, and Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari testified that every imprecation was fulfilled. This hadith serves as a key Shi'a proof-text for the legitimacy of Ali's succession and the consequences of suppressing prophetic testimony.
